text:
Mira Patel: Customer (AcmePay) opened an urgent lane — after their IdP cert rotation some users get immediate 401/Invalid Recipient when SSOing. They say it started right after rotation at ~02:17 UTC. They attached a failing SAMLResponse.

Alex Chen: Can you paste the raw Recipient/AssertionConsumerServiceIndex from their SAMLResponse? Also when you say rotated do they have dual-key metadata published?

Customer Support: They uploaded the SAMLResponse (base64) and the IdP metadata. Quick summary: IdP is now returning AssertionConsumerServiceIndex=\"1\" and Recipient=https://app.acme/pay/saml/consume (no trailing slash). Our SP metadata lists https://app.acme/pay/saml/consume/ (with trailing slash) as ACS index 1. Some users still succeed.

Rajiv Singh: Interesting — if Index is present we pick by index and don't compare Recipient string. Which log prints 'Invalid Recipient'?

Mira Patel: Runtime auth log snippet from sp-auth (redacted):
```
ERROR AuthHandler - invalid recipient mismatch: expected=https://app.acme/pay/saml/consume/ received=https://app.acme/pay/saml/consume
stack=AuthHandler.handleAssertion -> RecipientCheck
```
This shows we are doing a strict exact match even when index is used. I repro'd locally by POSTing a crafted SAMLResponse with ACSIndex=1 and Recipient without trailing slash.

Alex Chen: That suggests a codepath bug: when AssertionConsumerServiceIndex is set we should map index->ACS URL and then apply normalization tolerant checks (strip trailing slash, normalize http/https, host case) before strict reject. Looks like normalization is skipped.

Customer Support: For context: they run an Okta rotation that published new metadata with two KeyDescriptors (old and new). Metadata fetcher may have briefly returned stale metadata and matched index incorrectly for some requests — could explain intermittent success.

Support Bot: Ticket INC-2026-147 created and added eng-saml, idp-team.

Alex Chen: Quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily publish a duplicate ACS entry without trailing slash (fast, but manual), 2) push a canary hotfix to relax recipient comparison to accept both with/without trailing slash, 3) force IdP to use ACS URL matching our exact metadata (ask customer). Which is fastest?

Rajiv Singh: Option 2 is fastest for us (small change in RecipientCheck). We'll do a canary in prod and monitor 5xx/401s for that tenant. Also add extra logging in metadata watcher to record which metadata version was used per request (helps correlate with dual-key race).

Mira Patel: I asked the customer to try using ACS with trailing slash while we roll a canary. They uploaded the SAMLResponse (base64) so eng-saml can validate signature. Also requested their metadata URL and the time of rotation.

Alex Chen: I'll prepare a tiny patch: tolerantRecipient=true for the index path and a feature flag gated to the tenant. Will push to canary channel and then promote if green. Mira — can you prod acme to provide a failing base64 SAMLResponse and their IdP metadata URL (we need both old and new for correlation)?

Mira Patel: Sent a follow-up asking for both metadata URLs and the base64 SAMLResponse. Customer replied with timing & uploaded files. Forwarding to eng-saml now. Thanks :pray:

Rajiv Singh: After canary we should also add a regression test: SAML assertions with ACSIndex set and Recipient variants (trailing slash/no trailing, encoded querystring, port present). Add to saml-integration tests.

Alex Chen: Agreed. I'll add the test and the logging change. Will update ticket INC-2026-147 with deploy timeline.

Mira Patel: Noted. Marking customer as notified. Closing loop after canary verification.
